for: Everyone has a blood type and half-remembers it. The hook shows what a mismatched transfusion does (clumping), the middle shows why in real 3D (sugar antigens, IgM antibodies, the Rh protein), and the closing chart lets people find their own type; they send it to the family group chat to compare.
title: Why the wrong blood type is dangerous: antigens, antibodies and who can give to whom
question: What's your blood type?
send: Send this to your family group chat 🩸
credit: 3D red blood cells, antigens and antibodies: made in Blender for Anatomy Ace
why: Blood type is set by two markers (antigens), A and B, on the red cells, plus the Rh factor (RhD): present is positive, absent is negative. Group A has anti-B antibodies in the plasma, group B has anti-A, group O has both and AB has neither; the wrong ABO group can be life-threatening. US share (American Red Cross): O+ 37-38% (most common), A+ about 1 in 3, B+ about 9%, O- 7%, A- 1 in 16, AB+ under 4%, B- under 2%, AB- under 1% (rarest). O negative is the universal red cell donor; AB positive is the universal recipient; Rh-negative patients get Rh-negative red cells. For plasma the rules are reversed: AB plasma can go to any type. In a mismatched (ABO-incompatible) transfusion the patient's anti-A or anti-B antibodies, mostly IgM, bind the donor red cells, clump them (agglutination) and destroy them (hemolysis).
hook_pill: TYPE A BLOOD  →  TYPE B PATIENT

beats.say: Give someone the wrong blood type, and this happens.
Their antibodies grab the new red cells, clump them together, and destroy them.
label: CLUMPING
clump

beats.say: Every red cell wears sugar markers called [antigens](ˈæntɪdʒənz).
label: SUGAR ANTIGENS
sugar

beats.say: AB carries both. O carries neither.
label: A + B
sugar

beats.say: Your plasma makes antibodies against the ones you lack.
label: ANTIBODY (IgM)
antibody

beats.say: Type [A](ˈeɪ) has anti-B. Type B has anti-A. O has both.
Then there's the Rh protein. Have it, you're positive. Lack it, you're negative.
label: Rh (D) PROTEIN
rh

beats.say: O negative has no [A](ˈeɪ), no B, and no Rh,
so almost anyone can get its red cells. The universal donor.
label: UNIVERSAL DONOR
hero

beats.say: AB positive has every marker, so it can take red cells from any type. The universal recipient.
label: EVERY MARKER
sugar

beats.say: Plasma is the reverse: AB plasma can go to anyone.
label: NO ANTI-A, NO ANTI-B
plasma

beats.say: Nearly 4 in 10 Americans are O positive. AB negative is the rarest, under 1 percent.
